faq: How much should I spend on boosts?
Small amounts can show results. We often suggest a few dollars a day per post, set with your own cap. You choose the number, and your spend is billed by the platform, not by us.
It can bring attention to your posts, but it is not for buying followers or likes. We do not use any service that sells fake engagement, and we focus on real people who may become customers.
Is boosting the same as running full ads?
Not quite. Boosts promote an existing post. Full ads give more control over goals, placements and creative. We explain when to move up, and we can quote it from our Meta ads service.
Do all posts qualify to be boosted?
Posts must follow ad policies, so those with banned claims or restricted content are not eligible. We check this first and tell you if a favorite post needs an edit.

desc:
You can boost posts with small ad budgets when a post already earns attention and deserves a wider audience. Ecom Swift LLC chooses the right posts, sets the audience, goal and cap in your own ad account, and reports what the test cost and returned.

## What does it mean to boost a post?

Boosting a post means paying a social platform to show an existing post to more people than your followers alone. You choose who should see it, what action you want and how much you will spend. Because the post has already been published, you are promoting something that real people have reacted to, which lowers the guesswork compared with a brand new ad.

## Why a small budget needs careful setup

A small budget leaves little room for error. If the audience is too broad, the money is spread across people who will never care. If the goal is wrong, you may pay for views when you wanted visits to your store. If no end date is set, spending can continue longer than planned.

The quick boost button on many apps hides most of these choices. It is fast, but it offers limited control over placement, audience and goals. That is why we use proper ad campaigns inside your ad account, with a clear cap and end date, instead of the one-tap shortcut.

## How boosts influence reach and results

A boosted post can reach people who have never heard of you but resemble your buyers. Retargeting can also bring back people who watched a video or engaged with a post. Both can raise awareness, website visits or messages, depending on the goal chosen.

Results depend on the post itself, the offer, the audience and the market, so we cannot promise a set number of clicks or sales. What a short test does give you is evidence. You learn which posts, audiences and goals cost less and which are not worth repeating.

## What a good boost setup includes

- A review of recent posts to find those with real engagement.
- A single clear goal for each post, such as visits, messages or video views.
- An audience built from interests, location and past engagers.
- A daily or total budget cap and a firm end date.
- Placement choices that suit the format of the post.
- A check that the post follows ad policies, including text and image rules.
- Tracking on any link, so you can see visits from the boost.
- A mid-test look at results, with budget moved to better performers.
- A plain results note on cost, reach and clicks.
- A repeat plan based on what the test showed.

## What we do

We review your recent posts and pick the ones with the best signals, such as saves, shares and thoughtful comments. We set up each boost in your own ad account, working as an advertiser or partner, and run it for a short, agreed test window. We watch the early numbers and adjust where the package allows.

The Basic package boosts two posts with one audience and a capped budget. The Standard package boosts more posts across two audiences, picks a goal per post and includes a mid-test budget move. The Premium package runs a week-long program, tests extra audiences, retargets video viewers and ends with a comparison table and a review call. Ad spend is paid directly to the platform from your own account, separate from our fixed price.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Start with posts that already attract genuine comments and saves.
- Keep the offer and landing page clear and consistent.
- Set a spending cap before the boost starts.
- Give the test enough days for the platform to learn.
- Write down what you learned for next time.

**Avoid:**
- Boosting a weak post in the hope it improves.
- Targeting everyone, everywhere.
- Changing the audience and budget every few hours.
- Judging results after a single day.
- Buying followers or engagement from outside services.

## Who this is for

This service suits a small shop with a few strong posts and no ad experience. It suits a business that tried the boost button, spent money and could not tell what happened. It also suits an owner who wants to test the idea of paid reach before committing to a full ad campaign.

## What we need from you

We need access to your page and ad account as an advertiser, partner or admin role, given through the platform's own sharing tools. We never need your password. Please also set up a payment method in your ad account, share your goal and a rough weekly limit you are comfortable with, and tell us about any posts that must not be promoted.
